title: Research basics
summary: Everything for your first research project or final-year thesis: research questions, literature search, referencing, methods and writing.
description: Almost every degree ends with a project or dissertation, and most students meet research methods for the first time just before it. This roadmap takes you from a vague topic to a submitted, properly referenced write-up.

stages.title: Frame the question
stages.summary: Pick a topic and turn it into a question you can answer.

stages.title: Find and read
stages.summary: Search the literature, read it critically and keep track of sources.

stages.title: Do and write
stages.summary: Choose methods, collect and analyse data, and write it up.

nodes.title: Choosing a topic and research question
nodes.description: Narrow an interest into a specific, answerable question that fits your time, skills and data access, and agree it with your supervisor early.

nodes.title: Research ethics
nodes.description: Any project involving people or their data needs informed consent, confidentiality and usually approval from your institution's ethics committee before you start.

nodes.title: Searching the literature
nodes.description: Use Google Scholar and your library's databases with well-chosen keywords and filters, and follow the references of the best papers you find.

nodes.title: Reading papers critically
nodes.description: Read abstract, figures and conclusion first, then decide whether the paper deserves a full read. Judge the methods before trusting the results.

resources.title: How to Read a Paper (S. Keshav, PDF)

nodes.title: Referencing and reference managers
nodes.description: Use a reference manager from day one so citations and bibliographies are generated for you in your department's style (APA, Harvard, IEEE, Vancouver).

nodes.title: Research methods
nodes.description: Choose qualitative, quantitative or mixed methods based on your question, and justify your design, sampling and data collection.

resources.title: Research Methods: Plan and Evaluate Research Studies (Coursera)

nodes.title: Analysing your data
nodes.description: Learn the descriptive and inferential statistics your design needs, or a coding approach for qualitative data, and use free tools to run the analysis.

nodes.title: Writing up your project
nodes.description: Structure the report (introduction, literature review, methods, results, discussion, conclusion), write in drafts, and leave time for your supervisor's feedback.
